objectClass.notes: Static monumental landmark building, exterior shell only. No interior geometry: a prop kit is only ever looked at from outside, so an interior costs draw calls, geometries and VRAM for something nobody sees. Nothing moves, so one root pivot and zero sockets is the correct contract. An Isan ruin, and the registry notes are unusually specific about what that means: it is authored as partly collapsed with fallen blocks on the platform rather than as an intact building, because ruination is the state it is actually found in and is what distinguishes it. A red laterite platform of two courses of big blocks with a projecting stair bay between two cheeks, a low enclosure wall of individual blocks standing inside its edge, broken at the stair head and missing blocks; a squat sandstone tower on a moulded plinth, its plan the Khmer one -- corner bundles, recessed walls, a projecting door bay on each face carrying ringed colonnettes, a carved lintel and a naga-frame pediment; ONE real doorway recessed into the mass and three false doors; a three-band entablature flaring wider than the body; two roof tiers each a miniature sanctuary with its own aedicule per face; a broken top ring; thirty-six blocks lying where they fell; and grass in the joints. It is deliberately a separate asset from the Thai prang: squat, dark and rough where the prang is tall, slim, pale and encrusted.

reasoning: The identity is RUINATION, and ruination has to be geometry: a partial top ring with one corner gone, the acroterion of that corner missing below it, thirty-six blocks lying on the ring, the ledges and the platform, and an enclosure wall of individual blocks with members missing.

The plan is the Khmer plan -- stepped corner bundles, a recessed wall, a projecting door bay -- so every slab is one closed 52-point polygon rather than crossed boxes: correct shape, and no interior coincidence. The lower body slab additionally carries the doorway's NOTCH on +Z, so the one real doorway is a 1.05 m recess into the mass with the body's own stone for reveals.

The surface is the second half of the identity: the plate's two stones are coursed, the laterite is pitted and its blocks eroded at the arris, and the sandstone is streaked black on its sides and crusted orange on its ledges. All of it is five post-construction canvas tiles on the measured materials, not a texture set, with the ledge tops split onto their own material so a top and a side can differ.

Repetition is twelve-fold on the door units (four faces of the body and four of each roof tier, the tier ones the same geometry non-uniformly scaled), 36-fold on the debris, 56-fold on the enclosure wall's blocks and 24-fold on the grass tufts, and all of it is instanced. The debris and the broken block wall are the whole difference between a building and a ruin and they cost one draw call each.
Action readiness is minimal: static landmark geometry, box collider, and explicitly NOT breakable -- the collapse is modelled in, and the prop does not come apart further at runtime.

specDepthDecision.rationale: Six repetition systems against a ceiling of sixteen draw calls and SIXTEEN unique geometries. Thirty-six fallen blocks and fifty-six wall blocks as separate meshes would be ninety-two geometries -- over the ceiling many times before the building exists -- so each set is one InstancedMesh with authored (blocks) or seeded (wall) transforms.

coordinateFrame.notes: Origin base-center as the asset declares, +Y up. The prop is four-fold symmetric except for the stair bay, the one open doorway and the collapse, which are on fixed elevations: bay and doorway on +Z, the fallen corner at (+X, -Z). The tower is authored at the origin and every node is shifted -0.70 m in z at the end so the bay-extended bounding box is centred; the collider centre carries the opposite offset.

silhouette.description: A two-course laterite platform to 1.38 m with the stair bay projecting 1.4 m on +Z and a block enclosure wall to 2.06 m standing inside its edge, a moulded plinth to 2.05, a squat sandstone tower 5.64 m across to 5.05 m on the Khmer plan, a three-band entablature flaring to 7.16 m across between 5.05 and 6.60, a first tier to 7.35 at 5.7 m with a cap ledge to 7.52, a second tier to 8.32 at 5.1 m, a partial top ring to 8.72 at 4.84 m, and a heap of blocks reaching 9.00 m. The silhouette events are the broken block enclosure, the flare of the entablature, and above all the BROKEN outline of the top -- an intact tier would read as a different building.
silhouette.envelopeDerivation: x spans -5.30..+5.30 = 10.60, the bottom laterite course of a SQUARE platform; z spans 12.00 because the stair BAY projects 1.40 m off the +Z face (platform face at 5.18, bay to 6.70) and the whole model is shifted 0.70 m in z so the bounding box is centred on the origin. Both come from the Meshy proxy's bounding box, 1.68 x 1.429 x 1.90 units at the declared 9 m height: 1.68 x 9 / 1.429 = 10.6 across and 1.90 x 9 / 1.429 = 12.0 deep. The width was re-declared 12 -> 10.6 on 2026-09-02 with that arithmetic in the registry notes. y spans 0.00 to exactly 9.00: the top is a FALLEN BLOCK, the first entry of the authored placement list, lying on the broken ring's -X run top at 8.72 with sy 0.56 of a 0.50 m unit, so its upper face is at 9.00 by construction.
silhouette.meshyCrossCheck: Independent Meshy v7 reconstruction of the same plate normalises to w:h:d = 1 : 0.850 : 1.130, and the declaration is now 10.6 x 9 x 12 = 1 : 0.849 : 1.132 -- the envelope was re-declared FROM the proxy this build. Area-weighted band comparison gives mean |delta width| 0.035 and |delta depth| 0.024 of height (second build 0.041 / 0.055), with bands 3-9 -- the whole tower -- inside 0.03 H and no band past the 0.12 flag. The tower stack was re-read off the +Z orthographic depth map (96.7 px/m) for the door, plinth and body, and then CORRECTED by the band table for the roof: the depth map put the entablature at 5.90-6.75, and band 6 (5.4-6.3) measured -0.094 H against it; the table puts the flare from 5.05 and the widest band at 6.05-6.60, and the second tier stepping in to 5.1 m, which measured -0.025 / +0.009. The residual sits in bands 0-2 (-0.04 / -0.10 / -0.08 in width), the platform-and-enclosure zone, where the 5-95 percentile is dominated by the platform TOP's area rather than its edge and the proxy's enclosure is open on the stair side where the plate shows it closed.

viewEvidence.note: NOT DIRECTLY OBSERVED, and the lowest rear-view confidence of the monumental set. The tower is four-fold symmetric, but a RUIN is not: which corners have fallen and where the blocks lie on the unseen side is unknowable from one view, and the far side is authored as a plausible continuation rather than a measurement.

repetitionSystems.name: Enclosure wall blocks

placement.note: Seeded running bond around a 9.64 m square at outer face 4.82, two 0.34 m courses from 1.38, block lengths 0.85-1.20 m, thickness 0.72; the +Z run open for 3.8 m at the stair head; every ninth second-course block and one in twenty-five of the rest omitted; each block yawed, tilted and offset by a centimetre or two.

repetitionSystems.rationale: The plate's enclosure is plainly individual blocks with an irregular top, and the second build's textured box read as brickwork. Fifty-six blocks at one draw call and one geometry, each carrying one of five laterite tones through setColorAt and ONE cell of the coursing tile.
repetitionSystems.zFightingNote: Second-course blocks sit 2 mm lower than their nominal course, and every block has its own height scale (0.94-1.02), so no two undersides or tops share a plane; the run ends stop 3 cm short of each other.

repetitionSystems.name: Door colonnettes and jambs

placement.note: Four at radius 0 yawed a quarter turn each for the body; four per roof tier at (0.42, 0.16, 0.42) and (0.34, 0.14, 0.34) scale, pushed out so the scaled wall plane lands on the tier's own face.

repetitionSystems.rationale: Two ringed colonnettes (twelve-segment cylinders with four collars each, on square bases under square capitals) and two jambs merged into one unit. The plate's door is the most recognisable thing on the tower after its outline, and the tiers repeat it in miniature -- which is what makes the roof read as a stack of shrines rather than a stepped box.
repetitionSystems.zFightingNote: Jambs run 6 cm into the plinth top and 2 cm into the body face; the colonnette bases are buried 4.5 cm; the capitals' tops meet the lintel's underside as an opposed pair.

repetitionSystems.name: Carved lintels and pediments

placement.note: The same twelve transforms as door-frames.

repetitionSystems.rationale: A 2.62 x 0.46 m lintel beam 0.30 proud and a 2.50 m pointed pediment plate 0.22 proud, on their own material so the relief atlas can be bound without wrapping. The second build recorded the carving as below the resolvable band; at the distance the door is read from, the lintel is the darkest, busiest band on the face and its absence read as a garage.
repetitionSystems.zFightingNote: The lintel's back is buried 4 cm in the body and the pediment's 4 cm; the pediment stands on the lintel as an opposed pair and stops 3 cm under the first entablature band.

repetitionSystems.name: Blind door panels

placement.note: Three body faces (the +Z face is the real doorway) plus all four faces of each tier at the tier scales.

repetitionSystems.rationale: THREE on the body, not four. A Khmer sanctuary has one cell and false doors on the other three faces, so the set is deliberately not a full quad: the first of the four rotations is the identity and that face is left for the real doorway. The tiers have no cell, so all four of their faces are blind.
repetitionSystems.zFightingNote: Each leaf stands 0.10 m PROUD of the bay face with a central rib and a lock rail 0.05 m prouder again. Flush and the same stone as the wall, they were invisible: with no colour to spend, depth is what says door.

repetitionSystems.name: Fallen blocks

placement.note: Twelve on the truncated top (six on the broken ring, six heaped inside it, one of those on another), five slid down the ledges under the fallen corner, sixteen on the platform floor including one stacked on another, one fallen into a gap in the wall, one still up on the wall, one on the ground by the stair; every transform authored, every one resting on a named surface.

repetitionSystems.rationale: This is the component that makes the prop a ruin rather than a building, and it costs ONE draw call and ONE geometry. As thirty-six meshes it would exceed the sixteen-geometry ceiling on its own, before the building existed.
repetitionSystems.zFightingNote: Every instance carries its own yaw, tilt and NON-UNIFORM scale, authored per block, and is sunk a distinct 4-41 mm into whatever it lies on, so no two undersides share a plane with each other or with the tower's base. A raycast from every block's four bottom corners (scratch/_mon/support.mjs, now applied in world space) reports every corner within 5 cm of support except the one block on the ground, which the tool cannot see the ground under.

repetitionSystems.name: Grass tufts

placement.note: Six on the entablature ledge, three on the cap ledge, twelve on the platform floor, three on the wall tops; every position authored.

repetitionSystems.rationale: Five tapering blades leaning sideways in their own planes, ten triangles, one geometry, one draw call. The plate's ruin is overgrown at every ledge and the registry's texture prompt asks for grass in the joints.
repetitionSystems.zFightingNote: Each tuft is sunk a distinct 1.5-2.9 cm so its base shares no plane with a block's underside.

merge static components and reduce local feature geometry

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Real-time browser FPS prop on low-end integrated GPUs; a level builder places hundreds at once. All four ceilings come from thaikit resolveBudget() for the hero2x class and none was invented. The component split was costed against the DRAW-CALL ceiling in the blockout, before any geometry existed: parts that share a material are merged into one component rather than left to be merged later, because a pivot hung off a part cannot be merged afterwards.

drawCalls.note: Five components and six repetition systems: 11 of 16. The platform folds eleven parts into one submission, the tower folds fourteen, and the six instanced sets fold 151 discrete parts into six.

materials.note: sandstone covers the tower sides, the broken tier, the door units AND the blind panels; ledge covers every horizontal of the same stone; carved the twelve relief plates; laterite the platform and lateriteBlock the wall; pale the rubble; void the cell; grass the tufts. Eight of sixteen materials.

uniqueGeometries.note: One per component plus one per repetition system. A scaled box is NOT a shared geometry -- the generator bakes real dimensions in via geometry.scale(), so every differently-sized box is genuinely distinct. Each InstancedMesh reuses a single geometry across all its instances, which is the whole point.

triangles.note: 11,188 of 16,000. The colonnettes are the only curved thing on the prop -- ten twelve-segment cylinders per door unit, twelve units -- and the rest is boxes and extruded plans. The scarce axis is UNIQUE GEOMETRIES at 11 of 16, which is why the debris, the wall and the tufts are one instanced geometry each.

lightingFromPhoto.notes: The plate is a flat studio lightbox: surfaces at 90 degrees to each other measure within a few levels, which is only possible under near-shadowless illumination. That is WHY the measured crop means are usable as albedo with little correction.
High fill ratio inferred from the shadow-side wall retaining full value.

The seamless backdrop acts as a large uniform environment. The thaikit harness supplies NO environment map, which is why every metal on this prop carries a metalness well below its physical value -- a metal with nothing to reflect renders black.
NO rim light in the plate. Recorded so a missing rim in the render is not read as a defect.
Exposure 1.0 with ACES filmic tone mapping; no exposure compensation is applied to the measured albedos and none is warranted.

NO contact or ground shadow in the plate -- it is a cut-out against a seamless backdrop. Recorded so the absence is not read as a missing feature. IN USE this is a floor-placed building and the HOST scene owns its contact shadow: castShadow ships enabled on every mesh and the factory defines no ground plane of its own.

proceduralStrategy.strategy: Extrusions of closed plans and boxes, plus one pediment profile extruded along Z and the colonnette cylinders. The Khmer plan is a 52-point polygon (56 with the doorway notch); both it and the platform are single closed shapes rather than crossed boxes, which is both the correct shape and the only construction with no interior coincidence.

Six InstancedMesh systems carry 151 of the prop's discrete parts. The fallen-block and enclosure systems are the important ones: ninety-two instances with their own rotation, non-uniform scale and tone, at two geometries and two draw calls.
All procedural variation is assigned by instance INDEX, never from a random source, so the model is byte-identical on every build.

Every material is declared textureless to the GENERATOR -- no five-canvas procedural set. Five Canvas 2D tiles (laterite coursing, arrises and pitting; sandstone ashlar, drift and black washes; ledge flags, soil, moss and two lichens; the carved relief atlas; rubble mottle) are drawn post-construction as a few hundred Path2D fills at 512 px each and bound as map and bumpMap inside a factory that builds in ~90 ms. Every tone on them is a display-space ratio of the material's measured colour. The sandstone and ledge materials are re-based to the lichen envelope so the crusts can be BRIGHTER than the stone.

risks.description: Which corners have fallen and where blocks lie on the unseen side is authored, not observed. This is the lowest rear-view confidence in the monumental set at 0.55.
risks.mitigation: A tower is four-fold symmetric but a RUIN is not, so symmetry cannot close the gap the way it does on the chedi. The far side is authored as a plausible continuation of the observed pattern and is recorded as such rather than presented as measurement.

risks.description: The lintel frieze and the naga frame are procedural ornament in the plate's grammar, not a reproduction of the plate's particular carving.
risks.mitigation: At the distance a level is played from the frieze reads as a dark busy band with a central medallion and the pediment as a scalloped pointed frame, which is what the plate reads as; the atlas is also the bump map so it reads in relief.

risks.description: Band-table bands 0-2 (the platform and enclosure) read 0.04-0.10 H narrower than the proxy in width while the tower's bands 3-9 are inside 0.03 H.
risks.mitigation: The band's 5-95 percentile is dominated by the platform TOP's area rather than its edge, and the proxy's enclosure is open on the stair side where the plate shows it closed; the platform's outer extent is the proxy's own bounding box.

risks.description: check-coplanar flags five bounding-box pairs between the tower's side mesh and the ledge-top mesh.
risks.mitigation: They are one solid split by facing: the flagged planes are the side mesh's bounding-box extents against the top mesh's, whose faces are perpendicular, not co-facing. The check compares bounding boxes only and cannot tell.

risks.description: The black weathering ships at 0.33 of the clean stone against a measured 0.42, i.e. slightly darker, and the doorway cell at #3A2E24 against a measured near-black.
risks.mitigation: Both hold the turntable gate on chroma (0.000-0.005% enclosed background at four azimuths); the darker black is what gives the streaks the contrast the plate has at prop distance once the washes are blurred.
